scope: All 34 residual udovletvor-/udovolja mathematical-satisfaction sites in live v019 Latin sources, all in base-papers1-43-isv.tex.
choice: Complete the established EDIT-0038 policy by rendering every residual formal satisfy/fulfil predicate with official type-1 izpolnjati/izpolniti morphology and by recasting inherited dative or relative complements into grammatical transitive accusative constructions.
motivation: Every residual site concerns an equation, relation, condition, algebraic number, basis, or formal definition. Leaving a second Russian-shaped udovletvor- layer would preserve exactly the dominant-language collapse that v019 is correcting. A stem-only replacement would leave ungrammatical case government, so each complete clause was resolved at its exact predecessor line.
alternatives_rejected: Keep udovletvor- as an intelligible regional synonym: it is not the pinned official bridge chosen for this mathematical sense and would retain an avoidable East-Slavic layer.
Change only the predicate stem: this would preserve dative and relative government inherited from the rejected construction.
Use zadovalj-: the official family also covers pleasing or making content and was already rejected for formal mathematical fulfilment in EDIT-0038.
Defer the 34 sites for later human review: this edition is required to resolve known defects before handoff rather than export them as work for a future reviewer.

controlling_precedent.relevance: Established izpolnjati/izpolniti and accusative government for the same formal mathematical satisfaction sense.

official_dictionary.accepted_entries: id 597 izpȯlniti and id 2501 izpȯlnjati, both type 1; id 36609 izpȯlnjeńje
official_dictionary.rejected_entries: id 444 zadovaljati and id 3356 zadovoliti cover satisfy/please rather than the narrower formal fulfilment policy

official_verb_grammar.relevance: Aspect, present-stem contraction, and inflection of the accepted verb family.

german_semantic_authority.semantic_classes: Formal satisfaction of equations, relations, conditions, and definitions; no human-contentment sense.
